title: Keynes's 15-Hour Week
summary: John Maynard Keynes (1930) predicted productivity would make 15-hour workweeks possible by 2030 — and worried about what we'd do with leisure.
body:
Postscarcity economics studies what happens when automation and energy make goods abundant: UBI experiments, the economics of free digital goods, and the serious arguments about a post-scarcity future.

John Maynard Keynes (1930) predicted productivity would make 15-hour workweeks possible by 2030 — and worried about what we'd do with leisure. Productivity arrived; the leisure didn't. The essay frames every postscarcity debate.

title: UBI: The Idea
summary: Universal Basic Income: unconditional cash to everyone.
body:
Universal Basic Income: unconditional cash to everyone. Arguments: poverty elimination, bargaining power, automation dividend. Variants: negative income tax (Friedman), universal dividend (Alaska).

title: UBI Experiments: What We Learned
summary: Finland (2017-18): 2,000 unemployed got 560 euros/month — wellbeing up, employment flat.
body:
Finland (2017-18): 2,000 unemployed got 560 euros/month — wellbeing up, employment flat. Kenya (GiveDirectly): long-term UBI increased assets and earnings. Stockton, CA (SEED): employment rose. Evidence is mixed but real.

title: The Automation Displacement Debate
summary: Frey & Osborne (2013): 47% of US jobs at risk.
body:
Frey & Osborne (2013): 47% of US jobs at risk. Critics: tasks, not jobs, automate; new tasks emerge. The honest position: displacement is real and uneven; aggregate predictions are unreliable.

title: Care Work: The Last Scarcity
summary: Even in abundance, human care — nursing, teaching, therapy — resists automation.
body:
Even in abundance, human care — nursing, teaching, therapy — resists automation. Baumol's cost disease: productivity lags in human services, so their relative cost rises forever.
